newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. arms inspector complains of Iraqi interference.
newsitem.headline: U.N. arms inspector complains of Iraqi interference.

text.p: Chief U.N. arms inspector Rolf Ekeus has complained to the Security Council about Iraqi interference with U.N. helicopter flights during the inspection of several Iraqi facilities last week, council president Sergei Lavrov of Russia told reporters.
"We received a letter from the chairman of the Special Commission which will be discussed tomorrow when Mr. Ekeus is coming to the council to brief us, hopefully," Lavrov said.

Ekeus, executive chairman of the U.N. Special Commission in charge of scrapping Iraq's weapons of mass destruction, told the council in his letter: "In the last few days, there have been four serious incidents in which the lives of the crews of the commission's helicopters and the aircraft themselves were endangered through the actions of the Iraqi air personnel on board the aircraft or through the maneuvers of the accompanying Iraqi helicopter.
"These actions resulted in the air missions having to be terminated without successfully carrying out their tasks," added Ekeus, a copy of whose letter was obtained by Reuters.

In the first incident, on June 4, he said Iraqi air personnel threatened to shut off the helicpter's fuel pump and physically manhandled the U.N. chief air inspector and the U.N. commission's photographer to prevent them from taking photographs of the inspection site.

In the second incident, on June 5, one of the Iraqi personnel grabbed the co-pilot's control stick, resulting in the abortion of the mission. In the other two incidents, on June 7, an accompanying Iraqi helicopter placed itself in the path of the U.N. aircraft, forcing them to take radical evasive action, the letter added. It did not give the location of the Iraqi inspection sites or say why they were being scrutinized by U.N. weapons teams.
